post.description:
Check whether you already have a draft or submission for the specified asteroid, star, UTC date and station. Use this before repeating a submission.

The `found` field indicates the result:

- `observation`: a matching observation belongs to you. The `observation` field contains its ID, status, amendment count and web URL. If several match, the most recent is returned. The `event` field contains its attached event, if any.
- `event`: you have no matching observation, but an event matches the asteroid, star and date. The `event` field contains its ID and status.
- `none`: neither was found.

Other users' observations are not returned. Text matching ignores case and repeated whitespace. `asteroid_id` and `star_catalog` are compared only when supplied. Event lookup requires `asteroid_id`. Station is always compared; omitted, null and empty-string station values are equivalent.

event.summary: No observation of yours, but the event exists

post.summary: Check whether an observation already exists

post.description:
Create a draft and get an upload URL and form fields for each file. Upload each file directly to S3, then call `finalize`.

The Hub reads the observer, asteroid, star, time and result from the report spreadsheet or Tangra JSON report. These fields cannot be set in this request.

The optional `aperture_record` file can be a PyMovie `.pymovie` or Tangra `.lc` file, up to 500 MB.

For extra files such as plots or notes, use `slot: "attachment"` for each file. An observation can have up to 25 attachments, each up to 50 MB. Executables and scripts are not allowed. Save each returned `attachment_id` for finalization or removal.

get.description:
Get an observation or draft. Only the owner can read a draft; other callers receive `404`.

For drafts, `readiness` describes what is needed for submission, `checks` contains the latest check results (or null if checks have never run), and `next_actions` lists the next steps.

patch.description:
Update a draft's OWC link, asteroid confirmation, comments or required-file exemption. Fields omitted from the request stay unchanged. Changes start a new check run. Include the latest `version`; an outdated version returns `409 stale_version`.

The Hub tries to match an Occult Watcher Cloud (OWC) event after reading the report. Read `owc.resolution` for the result. To select an event yourself, set `owc_link_choice`:

- `picked`: set `owc_event` to an ID from `owc.resolution.candidates`.
- `pasted`: set `owc_event` to an OWC ID or URL. The Hub verifies it against OWC and the report.
- `proceed_unlinked`: continue without an OWC link.

Report fields cannot be edited here (`422 report_derived_fields`, with `details.fields`). OWC errors include `422 owc_not_a_candidate`, `422 owc_link_unparseable`, `422 owc_link_not_found`, `422 owc_link_mismatch` (with `details.violations`) and `503 owc_unavailable`.

post.description:
Save an uploaded file to the observation. On a draft, replacing the report updates the observation details read from it. The response's `report_parse` field indicates whether the report was read successfully.

When an owner replaces a submitted file, the API sets `amended_at`, increments `amendment_count` and changes the status to `amended`. A replacement report must identify the same asteroid, star, UTC date, result and station. Otherwise, the API returns `422 identity_changed`, lists the differences in `details.changed` and leaves the observation unchanged.

Once the event enters review, owner uploads are rejected with `409 already_processed`.

post.description:
Submit a draft and attach it to a matching or newly created event. Optionally send `version` to ensure the draft has not changed since you read it. An outdated version returns `409 stale_version`; omitting it submits the current version.

If the observation is already submitted, the request returns `200` with its current state.

Submission can fail with `422 missing_required`, `409 open_findings`, `409 checks_stale`, `409 stale_version`, `409 event_files_conflict` or `422 owc_link_mismatch`. The response's `details` identify missing items, open findings or OWC differences where applicable. Errors caused by the observation's state include `status`, `observation_id` and `amendment_count` in `details`.

An unresolved OWC link does not prevent submission. Check 11 is skipped when no link is available.

Another user's submitted observation returns `403 forbidden`; another user's draft returns `404 not_found`.

tags.description: Submit observations and retrieve events, observations and files through `/public/v1`. Send an API key in the `X-API-Key` header. Access is limited by your account permissions and the key scopes: `read` for reads and `observations:write` for writes. Use the API from scripts or servers; browser requests are not supported. To submit, create a draft, upload each file, finalize, wait for checks and submit. Within v1, existing response fields remain compatible and new fields may be added. API errors include `code`, `message`, `hint` and `details`. Use `code` in error-handling logic. Rate-limit responses include `Retry-After`.
tags.name: Public API v1
